cells.tense: You can point a direction and still leave the room free to walk it.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Pick a person close to you and a thing they're trying to get moving. Give the help it truly needs, and finish it this week, without being asked twice.
cells.core:
You know which way you're headed and you don't press it on anybody. Feeling with people is the ground you stand on, so when you hold a direction, those near you can sense the pull and stay themselves inside it. The alignment holds because nothing has to be surrendered for it.

What keeps this working is that the pull comes off you, so it doesn't need managing. Next time you open your mouth with your direction ready, stop before the whole case is made. Take a person you're close to and a thing they're trying to get off the ground: give what it actually needs and finish it, this week. The strength you hand across is what steadies the connection.
cells.sheetLine: Your direction stays yours while the room keeps theirs.
cells.place: where connection is felt and alignment is kept

cells.tense: You will be aiming people at a direction before anyone has arrived in it.
cells.act: sort the kinds of pull from one another
cells.ask: List every pull on you just now. Beside each, mark whose it is — yours to answer for, or picked up from someone close. Once, on paper, fixing nothing.
cells.core:
Where your direction meets people, the next move is already chosen and you're bracing for a landing nobody has seen. Each person gets felt for, and each also gets aimed. The connection it wants is the one happening now, not the one you've decided should happen next.

Before you commit to the next turn, take one evening and sort the pulls. Put each weight down on paper and mark whose it is — yours to answer for, or a charge someone close set on you. Nothing gets fixed. Seeing whose load is on you lets a borrowed one set itself down, and the direction that was yours from the start is easier to spot once the noise thins.
cells.sheetLine: You aim people at tomorrow before today has landed.

cells.tense: You knew a direction once and stopped standing where it could carry.
cells.ask: Go back to something you tended this past year that grew regardless — stand in front of it for a minute and take the pleasure of it.
cells.core:
You once pointed people toward somewhere better, and the pointing stopped. What you wanted to offer — the pull that carried those connections — can't reach from where you stand now. So you keep the sense of it to yourself while the conversation moves on past your turn: you know, and you go quiet after knowing.

It doesn't return by pointing harder into a place nobody is listening. Take something you tended this year that grew anyway, and go stand in front of what it became for a minute. Let yourself enjoy the result, because part of it is yours and nobody needs convincing. Rest there. From that spot the connections come back into view, and the direction becomes sayable when it does.
cells.sheetLine: You know the way and stopped saying it.

cells.tense: You are steadying a direction for people who cannot say where it came from.
cells.act: hold someone else up with what you have
cells.ask: Think of a person you've quietly held up. Tell them what you actually did to steady them — plainly, once, no compliment wrapped around it.
cells.core:
When you are at your best here, five people could tell you which way they're pointed and none of them could tell you who pointed them. You feel with people easily, so holding someone steady is close to automatic; you do it and forget you did. What you gave them keeps working, and the account of it says you were only standing by. You carry the bearing the way you carry a coat you forgot you had on.

Nobody needs correcting. Take a person you have quietly held up and give them what you actually did — not praise, one true piece, said plainly. It gets said once and nothing rearranges around it. What went unnamed gets its name back, and the pull you gave carries on with someone standing behind it now.
cells.sheetLine: You point the way and call it standing by.
cells.place: where connection is felt and alignment is kept
